variants.name: Kestrel (Commonwealth)
variants.description: Several years ago, while visiting a sweat lodge in search of spiritual renewal, Tarazed's chief ship designer fell into a trance and journeyed to a reality separate from our own. There he saw visions of a strange and elegant starship. Returning to his work with renewed purpose, he spent the next seven years making the Kestrel a reality.

variants.name: Finch (Commonwealth)
variants.description: When the Free Worlds started requesting a Carrier solution from its local shipyards, Tarazed Shipyards quickly saw that a few modifications could make their entry level interceptor into a top tier fighter. Over 85% of the parts that make up the Finch are shared with the Sparrow assembly line, so it's no surprise that even trimmed down to (barely) fit into a fighter bay, the blindingly fast Finch bears strong resemblance to its hyperspace-faring cousin. 	Fighters do not come equipped with a hyperdrive. You cannot carry a fighter unless you have a ship in your fleet with a fighter bay.

children.key: The people of New Britain and Wayfarer, and of all the Dominions and Territories thereunto belonging, are henceforth under the governance of the Commonwealth.
<first> <last> shall be, and is hereby declared to be, Lord Protector of the Commonwealth of New Britain and Wayfarer, and the dominions thereto belonging, for his life.
Considering your conquest of the Republic, Syndicate and the Free Worlds, the administration of the neutral Deneb zone bows to you in awe.
The citizens of Thule raise the song of freedom and their own existence as a people. Free from foreign bonds, may flourish the Free State and its citizens for many ages to come.

missions.name: ZOC: Bloodsea joins Free State
missions._internalId: LixiChronikouOrious list/Zone.of.Control::ZOC: Bloodsea joins Free State

children.key: You receive a message from the Free State Council: "Hail, thrice hail, our new President <first> <last>! Look down in mercy on us! Protect and guide the state, illuminate it from above!" You're not sure whether they take a joke at you, but as they'll pay and give provision to your ships for free, there's no reason to continue the hostilities.
Because of your aggression against the Free Worlds, your Militia license has been revoked by the Senate.

The Free Worlds' Senate is in disarray, but in a last effort they are able to agree in commissioning Alondo to negotiate peace with you. He can convince you to stop the hostilities in exchange for keeping all planetary tributes, and the restoration of your landing rights and licenses. At farewell you notice, that Alondo looks very very very disappointed in you.

You receive an encrypted message via the "Routed Onion Telemetrics" system. Only one person knows your onion address, so you transfer the message to a separate second-hand computer, type ******** into the password prompt, solve some tricky captchas personalized on information only you and the sender can know, like birthdays, pet fur color and endearments, insert your keys -- literal ones, not alphanumerical ones -- and finally have 30 seconds to read before the message destroys itself and the computer.

Ildy, now undisputed on Haven, informed you that she arranged a daily Voidcoin transaction worth of 700 credits a day as a compensation for your efforts, which nobody else she knew would have ever made for her. She'd like to send you more as a fair share of her "business", but that could become too conspicuous.
The tales of your good deeds throughout the Deep start to become part of Norn's folk culture, with the usual exaggerations.

You can't remember to have saved Skaldgar from falling into a volcano on Helheim, descending with a white-painted ship from a smoke-filled sky like an angel, triggering his regret and wish to make amends with his family. You doubt that you have melted through two kilometres of ice on Hope just to place Tosti's family stone.

And you assume that you would have known if you had fought Ice-Slugs on Nifel or Shark-Krakens on Windblain with bare hands. But at least you have saved a "maiden in distress", though you're pretty sure that Hjlod would scowl at how the story is told on Norn.
Anyway, the community councils decide to pay tribute to your contribution to Norn's society and culture, and will pay you a lifelong pension of 500 credits a day.
The government of Poisonwood decided to name you an honorary citizen, and to pay you a lifelong pension of 300 credits a day as a tribute to your role in the heroic liberation from the Alphas.
Because of your attack on the Republic, your Navy licenses have been revoked by the Parliament.

The Syndicate's supervisory board members are cornered in their last office tower. Your hostile takeover is complete, and grudgingly you're elected as chairman of the board. Your only obligation is to receive your wage in the form of tax-free tribute, and to leave the Syndicate alone.

The elders of the Skadenga and the Ranfolk voted to pay tribute to the deeds of Skadamarkadi, the one "marked by Skade", and to give support in the further voyage across the endless skies on the search of adventures to be besung in sagas which future generations will know as Edda Skadamarkada. May 800 credits a day be of good use on your path.
